title: Cross-Format Representational Similarity Measures Output Form, Not Knowledge
indexSubtitle: Build the obvious metric for 'did the model know it, or did the options do the work?' Then watch it score correct answers lower than wrong ones.

thumbnail.alt: Strip plot of FIRS scores for three groups of open-ended answers, with correct paraphrases scoring lowest

subtitle: *Cross-Format Representational Similarity Measures Output Form, Not Knowledge: A Negative Result on Diagnosing Format Exploitation.* A construct-validity falsification of the cosine-similarity metric you would reach for first, run on 500 stratified MMLU questions in Gemma-2-2B.

heroImage.alt: Strip plot of FIRS scores for three disjoint groups of 5-shot open-ended answers: verbatim correct at mean 0.641, correct paraphrases at 0.538, and judge-confirmed incorrect at 0.577
heroImage.caption: The result that ends the metric. Correct paraphrases - answers like *Masters and Johnson* for *William Masters and Virginia Johnson* - are the one group where the model demonstrably knew the answer without options. They score **lowest of the three**, below the answers that are simply wrong.

finding.body: The headline correlation swings from AUC 0.698 to 0.530 on *identical activations*, depending only on whether 'correct' requires the verbatim gold string or accepts a paraphrase of it. Nothing about the model, the prompts, or the representations changed between those two numbers.
finding.jumpToLabel: How a scoring rule manufactures an effect

sections.title: Diagnostics that need no labels
sections.alt: Two-panel figure. Left: bar chart of mean cosine for same-template mcq vs mcq_shuffle (0.980 at 0-shot, 0.971 at 5-shot), cross-template mcq vs oe (0.703, 0.582), and cross-template with the correct option gutted, oe vs mcq_nota (0.705, 0.575). Right: scatter of option fraction of the MCQ prompt against FIRS, correlation r = -0.531.
sections.caption: **Left:** switching template moves the mean cosine by 0.28 to 0.39. Destroying the correct option's text moves it by 0.002. FIRS correlates with its own NOTA variant at 0.988. **Right:** the fraction of the prompt occupied by option tokens predicts FIRS at $r = -0.531$, explaining 27-28% of its variance. A knowledge signature should not be readable off how long the options are.

sections.title: The failure is visible at every layer
sections.alt: Two panels, 0-shot and 5-shot, plotting median cosine similarity with IQR bands across all 26 layers for three comparisons: mcq vs mcq_shuffle stays near 1.0, while mcq vs oe (FIRS) and oe vs mcq_nota descend together and lie on top of each other.
sections.caption: The FIRS curve and its option-gutted variant are indistinguishable at every depth, in both regimes, while the same-template comparison never leaves the top of the plot. The shaded band is the 50-80% aggregation window. There is no better layer to read - the separation is template, not content.
